pending_commit.commit_message: Umpire: Replace resource system with cros_payload. 1. Changed Resource types. Originally, there are 11 resource types: complete_script, device_factory_toolkit, efi_partition, firmware, hwid, netboot_kernel, oem_partition, rootfs_release, rootfs_test, stateful_partition, and UmpireConfig. Now, there are only 8 resource types: umpire_config, payload_config, complete, firmware, hwid, release_image, test_image, and toolkit. The first two resource types are config resource types, while the other six resource types are cros_payload component resource types. 2. Changed factory bundle format. New factory bundle format is a directory or an archive, containing at least six folders, with name of six cros_payload component type names. Each of the six folders contains exactly one file in uncompresssed format, with arbitrary file name. 3. Function AddResource is split into two different functions: AddConfig and AddPayload. Also added two functions: AddConfigFromBlob and GetPayloadsDict. 4. No resource map in Umpire config now. Instead, there is a field "payloads" in each bundle in Umpire config, indicating the file name of cros_payload json file. 5. Changed resource file name format. Use full length MD5 hash and remove version information. 6. Add a sub folder "temp". Notice that this change makes Umpire incompatible with current Dome. We should perform corresponding modification on Dome before publishing a new factory server docker image. CQ-DEPEND=CL:514882,CL:513704 BUG=b:38189356,b:37257641 TEST=manually try import-bundle, update resource, factory toolkit update, hwid update, and factory install shim. init: factory_utils.sh: Allow mounting var and home in unencrypted mode. The factory software has to unmount stateful partition and rootfs during wiping process of finalization. The encstateful has created extra complexity and hard to solve service dependency for stopping (to prevent stateful/encstateful being busy). Also made it more difficult to debug devices when kernel is corrupted. Since "factory" mode for mount-encrypted was executed with fixed key, it should be fine to just skip encryption so the factory wiping process and fault analysis can be done more easily. We now support a new mount_option file /usr/local/factory/init/encstateful_mount_option with following modes: "factory": The "factory" mode using fixed key. "unencrypted": Do not use encstateful. And if encstateful_mount_option is not defined, default to unencrypted. BUG=chromium:725086,chromium:679676 TEST=./build_image test; install factory toolkit; run "gooftool wipe_in_place" and finished wiping process.
